doctrine: A board claim is never truth on its own. The evidence field carries the proof. The executor updates this JSON at every checkpoint and re-renders. A card may not enter status=shipped with evidence=null; a launch gate condition may not be state=pass with evidence=null. Enforced by docs/board/validate-board.mjs. GATE VOCABULARY on this project: green_self_merge = an executor terminal merges its own PR once the required checks are green (routine code and docs). ivan_merge = Ivan clears the merge - anything touching production data, money, credentials, security boundaries, or visual work he reviews on a deployed screen. adam_authorizes = the owner authorises before anything is built or spent - product decisions, paid-tier upgrades, account ownership changes. stakeholder = an outside party signs off (Shopify app review, a payment processor, counsel); reserved, no card carries it yet. MERGE AUTHORITY, granted by Ivan 2026-08-20 once branch protection went live on main (PRs mandatory, required checks typecheck + lint + build, no bypass): a green_self_merge card is merged by the executor terminal itself once ALL required checks are green, squash merge, branch deleted after. ivan_merge, adam_authorizes and stakeholder are unchanged and are never merged by an executor. If a card's gate field contradicts a verbal grant, THE BOARD JSON WINS: halt on that card and flag it. MERGING IS NOT SHIPPING. Non-visual work (SEC, CODE, INFRA, CHORE) ships on merge with the PR as evidence. Any UI or visual card ships only on Ivan's deployed-screen confirmation, whoever merged it, because a green check proves the code compiles, lints and builds and cannot prove a screen looks right. RED IS NEVER MERGED: a check that flakes or reddens is fixed or halted on, and disabling, relaxing or narrowing a check to obtain green is forbidden. See BOARD-SPEC.md, Merge authority. HOME_LANE IS A KIND, NOT AN ACTIVITY CLAIM: a card sits in in_flight because it is a work item on the active queue, and its status says whether anyone is executing it. Card census moves; read it from the validator output rather than from this sentence. DESIGN VERSUS CODE, set by Ivan 2026-08-20 with the W1 dispatch: when a design and the code disagree about FACTS (limits, counts, categories, quotas, prices) the CODE is the truth and the COPY is changed to tell the truth. When they disagree about INTENT (features, flows, whole screens) it becomes a card gated adam_authorizes. Design wins on VISUALS only. Never ship copy that promises what the code rejects. Copy that states a limit should read from the constant that enforces it, so a later ruling changes one value rather than a value and a sentence that drift apart. See BOARD-SPEC.md, Design versus code. AUTHORIZING-MESSAGE EXCEPTION, set by Ivan 2026-08-21: the board JSON normally wins over a verbal grant and a contradicting card is halted on, EXCEPT when the contradiction is between the JSON and the same message that AUTHORIZED the work. Then the message wins, the JSON is brought into line, and the source is recorded on each card changed. A gate that contradicts its own dispatch is stale JSON, not a competing instruction, and halting would stop the run the message exists to start. Halt-loud stays for every conflict the authorizing message does not itself resolve. COPY READS THE CONSTANT THAT ENFORCES IT, doctrine from 2026-08-21: wherever a limit, quota or count is DISPLAYED, the copy reads the constant that enforces it, never a literal in a sentence. A limit written twice eventually goes wrong in one place, and the copy is the half that rots, because the check keeps working and the screen quietly lies. When two screens enforce different values they STATE different values; making them agree is a product decision and belongs on a card. See BOARD-SPEC.md.

cards.title: /login submit returned the raw Supabase gateway error "Invalid path specified in request URL"; root cause was a malformed NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL, corrected by Ivan

evidence.ref: Ivan confirmed on deployed instance 2026-08-20, both logins green after env correction

cards.notes: Reported by Ivan 2026-08-20 against https://lablld-1.vercel.app: submitting /login showed "Invalid path specified in request URL". RESOLVED by an env correction on Ivan's side; he confirmed on the deployed instance that both an admin and a merchant account now log in cleanly. MECHANISM, re-derived from the installed code rather than transcribed: supabase-js 2.99.1 builds every sub-API URL by RELATIVE resolution against the env value (dist/index.mjs:367-398, new URL('auth/v1', ensureTrailingSlash(NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL))). Any path segment left in that variable is therefore preserved, the auth request lands on a route the Supabase gateway does not serve, and the gateway answers with exactly that string. The message reached the user's screen in English because translateAuthError (app/(auth)/actions.ts) had no branch for it and returned the upstream text unchanged. That display defect is fixed in the same PR that carries this card. REQUIRED SHAPE, variable name only: NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL must be scheme plus host and nothing else - no path, no /rest/v1 or /auth/v1 suffix, no dashboard URL. No secret value was read, requested, printed or logged at any point in this incident.

cards.title: /register crashed with "Application error: a client-side exception has occurred"; cleared by the same NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL correction, throw site never captured

evidence.ref: Ivan confirmed on deployed instance 2026-08-20, both logins green after env correction

cards.notes: Reported by Ivan 2026-08-20: /register threw "Application error: a client-side exception has occurred", a full crash rather than the intentional signup gating Adam described. The gating itself is configured in Supabase Auth and is NOT a defect; the crash was. RESOLVED: Ivan confirmed on the deployed instance that /register no longer crashes after the same NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL correction that cleared INC-01. The card closes on that confirmation. THE THROW SITE WAS NEVER CAPTURED AND IS RECORDED HERE AS UNPROVEN. The reported mechanism - the malformed URL throwing at the client factory's URL scheme check before network I/O - was tested locally against the installed @supabase/supabase-js 2.99.1 and @supabase/ssr 0.9.0 and is FALSIFIED, two independent ways. (1) @supabase/ssr delegates to the same supabase-js createClient (ssr/dist/main/createServerClient.js:16), so the URL shapes that DO throw at the scheme check - no scheme, empty, undefined - throw identically in all three factories. proxy.ts:8 constructs a client from that same variable on every matched request, and the matcher covers both /login and /register, so such a value would have failed at the edge and neither page would have rendered at all. (2) The only URL shape that produces INC-01's gateway response is a path-suffixed URL, and that shape was probed and constructs CLEANLY in all three factories; it never throws. One env value cannot both throw at the factory and reach the gateway. Since /login rendered and displayed a gateway message, the URL parsed. WHAT IS CERTAIN: the env correction cleared it, and this app has no error.tsx and no global-error.tsx anywhere in app/, so ANY uncaught throw renders that exact default message and names no location. WHAT IS NOT KNOWN: which statement threw. No server stack trace was taken, Vercel runtime log access is permanently off limits by Ivan's ruling of 2026-08-20, and the defect no longer reproduces. Do not build on the reported mechanism. MITIGATION SHIPPED WITH THIS CARD: the three auth entry points now reach the Supabase factories through lib/supabase/safe.ts and fail CLOSED with a Spanish message instead of throwing, and registerAction no longer discards the error from its merchants pre-check - a discarded error there read as "this email is free" and let registration proceed on an unknown answer. ACCEPTED TRADEOFF, stated rather than buried: the fix adds NO logging, because CLAUDE.md forbids console output and the repo holds that rule perfectly (zero console.* calls in app/, lib/, components/ and proxy.ts). A configuration failure is therefore now silent to the operator: the user sees a readable message and the app stays up, but nothing records why. Introducing a logging convention inside an incident hotfix was the wrong place to decide it. That gap belongs to INFRA-billing-alerting, which already owns "no error reporting anywhere in the codebase", and is noted on it. See also CODE-error-boundaries, the card that would have made this incident legible instead of anonymous.

cards.title: Add HMAC verification to /api/shopify/fulfillment_order_notification; it is an unauthenticated, unsigned service-role write path while its five sibling webhooks all verify
cards.notes: P0 · Source: docs/audit/CODE-AUDIT-2026-08.md R3. Launch gate G5 does not pass until this is closed. WORKED 2026-08-20 by PINK, PR #2, awaiting Ivan's merge (ivan_merge gate), so it is in_flight and not shipped: it flips to shipped with a pr evidence ref on merge. RE-DERIVED FROM CODE, AND THE CARD'S FRAMING IS INCOMPLETE. This is not one unsigned endpoint among five signed siblings. TWO routes handle this event, both registered on every OAuth connect, both performing the identical service-role write on orders: /api/shopify/fulfillment_order_notification, reached because registerFulfillmentService sets callback_url to {WEBHOOK_URL}/api/shopify (lib/shopify.ts:101) and Shopify appends the notification path; and /api/webhooks/shopify/fulfillment-order, registered for topic fulfillment_orders/fulfillment_request_submitted (app/api/shopify/callback/route.ts:55-59). Only the second verified. The second also carried its own INLINE dual-secret verifier, because the two registration paths are signed with different secrets: a programmatic topic webhook with SHOPIFY_API_SECRET, a Dev Dashboard registration with its own SHOPIFY_WEBHOOK_SECRET. FIX: that verifier is exported from lib/shopify.ts as verifyFulfillmentHmac and both routes now use it, so the boundary has one implementation instead of one implementation and one hole. NEITHER ROUTE DELETED: which of the two Shopify actually delivers to is a live-system fact and no LABLLD terminal has production access. Verifying both breaks nothing; deleting the wrong one silently breaks fulfillment tracking. PROVEN at authoring time against the real exported function, 6 cases green (valid under either secret accepts; attacker secret, absent header, short header, and a valid signature for a different body all reject) plus a NEGATIVE ARM: with the guard removed the forged request is accepted, which is what makes those assertions load-bearing. The probe becomes a committed test in INFRA-ci-and-tests, card 4 of this wave. OPEN RISK FOR IVAN: if Shopify's fulfillment-service callback carries no X-Shopify-Hmac-Sha256 header, this endpoint now 401s where it used to accept. Unverifiable from code. Mitigating fact: the signed sibling receives the same event and does the same write, so the column still gets populated; the failure mode is a redundant path going quiet, not lost data. Confirm after merge by connecting a store, placing a test order, and checking orders.shopify_fulfillment_order_id. Merged 2026-08-20 by Ivan (ivan_merge). Non-visual, so it ships on merge with the PR as evidence, per the merge-authority grant of the same day. STILL OPEN AND NOT A BLOCKER TO SHIPPING: whether Shopify's fulfillment-service callback carries an X-Shopify-Hmac-Sha256 header is unverifiable from code, and if it does not this endpoint now 401s where it used to accept. The signed sibling receives the same event and performs the identical write, so the failure mode is a redundant path going quiet, not lost data. Confirm by connecting a store, placing a test order, and checking orders.shopify_fulfillment_order_id.

evidence.ref: PR #9 merged and deployed; migration 0003_labels_bucket_private.sql applied by Ivan 2026-08-20; Ivan confirmed on the deployed instance: bucket private + all label surfaces render without errors; signed-URL happy path (upload -> store -> sign -> render) unverified, no label data exists yet. cards.notes: P1 · Source: audit §5 privacy finding; docs/db/SCHEMA-RECONSTRUCTION-NOTES.md C11; ruling 2026-08-20 (public authored for parity only, exposure not accepted). Launch gate G5 does not pass until this is closed. WORKED 2026-08-20 by PINK, code PR #9. in_flight, and it stays in_flight through the migration apply: per Ivan's sequencing the code ships first, he applies the bucket flip in the dashboard, he confirms labels still render on the deployed instance, and only then does this card ship. WHY THAT ORDER: a private bucket with getPublicUrl() still live returns 403 for every label, so labels would silently stop rendering for merchants and for admins working the approval queue. The deployed code signs every read AND falls back to the stored public URL when signing fails, so it is correct against a public bucket and a private one. That fallback is what makes the order safe rather than merely preferred. MIGRATION AUTHORED, NOT APPLIED: supabase/migrations/0003_labels_bucket_private.sql. It flips storage.buckets.public to false for labels and replaces the labels_read_all policy (which was `to public`, mirroring the bucket flag) with an owner-or-admin read. product-images is deliberately untouched. Ivan applies it in the dashboard; no LABLLD terminal touches a database. THE DESIGN DECISION THAT DEVIATES FROM THE CARD SCOPE, and the reason: the scope said migrate BOTH UPLOADERS to createSignedUrl. The uploaders were deliberately left alone, because label_url is an IDENTITY as well as a locator. Three sites match on its exact value: app/api/admin/labels/[id]/route.ts:56 does .eq('label_url', label.label_url) to approve or reject, app/admin/labels/page.tsx:46-48 keys a map on merchant_id:label_url, and components/merchant/label-picker.tsx:32 compares equality. Storing a signed, expiring URL would break label APPROVAL silently: the .eq() would match zero rows. Worse, product-stepper.tsx:32 seeds its state from label_url and saves it back through saveMerchantProductAction, so a signed URL would be PERSISTED into the database and expire there. The stored value therefore stays the canonical public form and signing happens at render only. If Ivan wants the stored form changed it is a data migration and a separate card. SIGNED AT: app/(merchant)/labels/page.tsx, app/admin/labels/page.tsx, app/admin/orders/[id]/page.tsx (the order-detail thumbnails), and app/(merchant)/orders/page.tsx which feeds the client order panel. PLUS ONE NOT IN THE CARD SCOPE AND EASY TO MISS: app/(merchant)/products/[id]/actions.ts hands label_url to SudoMock, which fetches it from OUTSIDE our network. A private bucket 403s the stored public form, so mockup generation would have broken. It is now signed with a shorter 10-minute TTL because that URL leaves our control. THREE no-img-element DEFERRALS FROM PR #5 RESOLVED, and one of them was resolved by correcting my own earlier reasoning. app/admin/orders/[id]/page.tsx and components/merchant/order-tab-panel.tsx now carry a permanent decision instead of a deferral: the src is a signed, expiring URL, so every render is a fresh optimizer cache miss and a fresh billable transformation, which makes next/image the wrong tool. The THIRD, components/merchant/product-step-label.tsx, was never a labels URL at all. It renders theme previews from the PUBLIC product-images bucket (theme-labels-editor.tsx:36 uploads there), so the reason I wrote in PR #5 was simply wrong. The comment now says so and hands it to the UI wave as an ordinary decision. The two existing next/image label usages gained `unoptimized` for the same cost reason, and because a signed URL's path is /storage/v1/object/sign/... which does not match the /storage/v1/object/public/** remotePattern in next.config.ts and would have 400d in the optimizer. SEEDED OR MOCK LABEL OBJECTS: NONE, confirmed from code paths as instructed. supabase/seed.sql contains zero references to merchant_products or merchant_labels; it inserts admin_emails and three products only. Nothing to migrate. DEAD CODE LEFT ALONE: components/merchant/label-picker.tsx, product-configure-form.tsx and product-label-panel.tsx all read label_url but are UNREACHABLE (product-configure-form has no parent and is LabelPicker's only importer). They are CODE-delete-dead-files' problem; polishing dead code would have widened this diff for no behaviour. PROVEN: labelObjectPath exercised directly, 6 cases, including the negative arm that a product-images URL returns null so the wrong bucket can never be signed. tsc, eslint --max-warnings=0 and a full next build all green locally. SHIPPED 2026-08-20. Ivan applied 0003 in the dashboard and confirmed on the deployed instance: labels bucket shows Private, product-images still Public, /labels renders clean and /admin/labels renders clean. WHAT WAS NOT PROVEN, recorded because the surfaces were empty and a clean render of an empty page proves less than it looks like it does: both label pages rendered their EMPTY STATE, because no label data exists yet, and the admin order-detail thumbnail was NOT TESTABLE because zero orders exist. cards.title: OAuth state is generated at app/api/shopify/auth/route.ts:23 and never verified; the callback reads it and discards it, so CSRF protection on the handshake is decorative (Shopify HMAC still applies)
cards.notes: P2 · Source: audit §8.5(b). ADDED-BY-SWEEP. WORKED 2026-08-20 by PINK, PR #8. in_flight, not shipped: the gate is ivan_merge and the board JSON wins over the self-merge grant, so this one waits for Ivan. Last of the six W0 cards. CARD CONFIRMED EXACTLY: state was generated with crypto.randomBytes(16) at app/api/shopify/auth/route.ts:23 and stored nowhere, so the callback had nothing to compare against. FIX: the auth route persists the state in an HttpOnly cookie and the callback compares in constant time, 403 on mismatch. The cookie name and the compare live in lib/shopify.ts so the two routes cannot drift. FOUR DELIBERATE DETAILS, recorded because each is a place where the obvious choice is wrong. SameSite=Lax not Strict: the callback is a cross-site top-level navigation from Shopify and Strict would withhold the cookie and break every install, so Strict is the more secure-LOOKING setting and the broken one. State is checked AFTER the HMAC check: HMAC proves Shopify sent it, state proves this browser started it, and the cheaper stronger one runs first. A FAILED CHECK DOES NOT CLEAR THE COOKIE: clearing on failure would let anyone break a real merchant's pending install by hitting the callback URL with a wrong state. It is single-use on every path PAST the check and expires on its own in ten minutes. Length is compared before timingSafeEqual because the caller controls the query parameter and timingSafeEqual throws on a length mismatch. PROVEN against the real exported function, 7 cases: genuine round trip accepts; attacker state, absent state, absent cookie, both absent, wrong length and a single changed character all reject. NEGATIVE ARM: with the guard removed the forged callback is accepted. SCOPE NOTE: the card says Shopify HMAC still applies, and that stays true. This was never an open door; the missing leg was the binding to the browser that started the flow. ALSO REMOVES the eslint-disable added in PR #5 for the unused state read. That marker existed to keep the hole visible; the hole is closed, so it goes. NEEDS A DEPLOYED CHECK, the one thing a unit probe cannot prove: connect a store from /settings/shopify end to end after merge. A 403 Invalid state means the cookie is not surviving the round trip. SHIPPED: merged by Ivan 2026-08-20 (ivan_merge). Non-visual, so it ships on merge with the PR as evidence. THE BIGGEST FIX NEEDS NO VENDOR AT ALL: the cron returned HTTP 200 even when every single charge threw, so Vercel’s cron monitor recorded a success and nobody was told. It now returns 500 when any charge failed. The platform already watches this endpoint’s status code, so making the status honest turns existing monitoring into the alert. THE CHARGES ARE NOT ROLLED BACK by that non-200 and the code says so: affected merchants are already marked past_due, the status reports the run rather than undoing it, and a retry is safe because each attempt re-reads who is still due. lib/ops-report.ts is the seam. Wired into the cron’s per-merchant catch and into lib/supabase/safe.ts, which is the auth-config path this card was explicitly extended to cover when INC-02 closed — a login failing on configuration used to leave no operator-visible trace at all. CLAUDE.md’S NO-CONSOLE RULE IS NOW ENFORCED RATHER THAN DOCUMENTED. It lived in a document and nothing checked it, which is the same shape of problem as a limit living in a sentence. no-console is an eslint ERROR now, with exactly one file exempted. NEGATIVE ARM: a console.log added to any other file reddens lint with "Unexpected console statement"; the same statement in lib/ops-report.ts passes. Widening that exemption is now a visible decision rather than a quiet habit. THE SEAM IMMEDIATELY EARNED ITS KEEP by exposing a latent bug nobody had seen: the first build after wiring it logged an auth.config failure for /reset-password that was really Next saying "this route is dynamic". safeServerClient was CATCHING Next’s control-flow throw — redirect, notFound and dynamic detection all signal by throwing with a digest — which is a bug dressed as resilience. Those are re-thrown now and never reported. A channel that cries wolf on every build is worse than no channel.

WHY IT IS NOT A UI CARD: no merchant delete path exists in code at all (app/(merchant)/products/actions.ts exposes only toggleMerchantProductAction), and order_items snapshots must survive the delete, which makes it a data-lifecycle problem wearing a button. NEEDS AN ADAM RULING BEFORE ANY BUILD: what happens to a merchant product that has live orders. Blocking the delete, soft-deleting, and cascading are three different products. order_items already snapshots product_name and unit_price at creation (migration 0001), so past orders survive a row deletion, but merchant_product_id is a restrict-on-delete FK, so a hard delete of a referenced row FAILS today rather than orphaning. That is the constraint any ruling has to answer to. W1 SHIPS INSTEAD: UI-my-products restyles the existing active/inactive toggle into the design's visual language. The danger zone is simply absent, not faked. RULED 2026-08-21 by Adam: SOFT DELETE. The merchant product is hidden from the merchant, order history is preserved intact, and the restrict FK stays in place as a safety net rather than being relaxed to a cascade. UNBLOCKED and moved into the W2 queue at P2, third in the run order. WHAT THE RULING IMPLIES FOR THE BUILD: the schema needs a deletion marker (deleted_at or is_deleted) authored as a migration file for Ivan to apply; every merchant-side read of their own products filters it out; admin reads are unchanged and still see everything. Gate changed from its authored value by the authorizing-message exception (BOARD-SPEC.md, 2026-08-21): Ivan’s W2 dispatch of 2026-08-21 both carries the ruling and grants self-merge on green throughout, so the message wins over the stale JSON. Migrations remain authored-not-applied. BUILT 2026-08-21 in PR #26. It adds a merchant-facing screen element (the danger zone), so it lands in_flight awaiting Ivan’s deployed-screen review rather than shipping on merge. MIGRATION 0005_merchant_products_soft_delete.sql IS AUTHORED AND NOT APPLIED — until Ivan applies it the deployed code writes to a column that does not exist and every delete fails; the reads that filter `deleted_at is null` fail too, which takes /products, /catalog and the dashboard with them. THIS ONE IS NOT SAFE TO DEPLOY AHEAD OF ITS MIGRATION, unlike 0003 and 0004. WHAT LANDED: softDeleteMerchantProductAction in app/(merchant)/products/actions.ts (ownership-checked, sets deleted_at and is_active=false, and drafts the Shopify listing exactly as the existing deactivate path does, because leaving a listing live in the merchant’s own store while it is gone from here would let a customer buy something we no longer show); eight merchant-side reads now filter deleted_at is null (/products, /catalog, /catalog/[slug], /products/[id], /products/[id]/edit, /dashboard, /orders/new page and action); ADMIN READS ARE UNTOUCHED, per the ruling, so an operator still sees everything; and ORDER HISTORY IS UNTOUCHED — /orders joins order_items to merchant_products and is deliberately NOT filtered, which is the whole point of soft over hard. THE UNIQUE CONSTRAINT (merchant_id, product_id) DELIBERATELY STAYS WHOLE rather than becoming partial on deleted_at: six call sites resolve a row with .maybeSingle() on that pair and would start throwing the moment a merchant held two rows for one product. The consequence, stated rather than discovered later: re-adding a deleted product REVIVES the original row with its old label, mockup and price, because saveMerchantProductAction finds it and clears deleted_at instead of inserting. If Adam would rather a re-add start blank, that is a product question and a follow-up card, not a bug. VERIFIED in an isolation harness: the danger zone renders with the design’s hairline divider, the confirm reads "¿Eliminar {nombre}?" then "Eliminar para siempre" in #C0303B, and Cancelar returns to the collapsed state. cards.notes: P2 · REPORTED 2026-08-21 by Ivan from the deployed instance: "create-flow stepper displays STEP 1 OF 6 on every step, observed on steps 5 and 6." INVESTIGATED THE SAME DAY AND NOT REPRODUCED. What the code actually does: components/merchant/product-stepper.tsx:153 renders `Paso {step} de {STEPS.length}`. Both halves are derived — the numerator is the component’s own step state, the denominator is the length of the STEPS array that also builds the rail above it — and there is no literal step number anywhere in the file, so there is no line that could hold a stale 1. HOW IT WAS CHECKED: a throwaway isolation harness route mounted the real ProductStepper with stub props at each initialStep; SSR emitted "Paso 1 de 6", "Paso 3 de 6", "Paso 5 de 6" and "Paso 6 de 6" correctly. Then in the browser, mounted at step 4 and driven forward through the two client transitions that reach the reported steps — Continuar → (goTo 5) and Omitir por ahora → (goTo 6) — the eyebrow read PASO 4 DE 6, then PASO 5 DE 6, then PASO 6 DE 6, and the rail advanced with it. The harness cannot drive the two transitions that call a server action first (step 1 → 2 and the label save at step 3 → 5), but neither action revalidates or redirects, so neither can reset client state. BLOCKED ON IVAN, deliberately: fabricating a fix for a defect that does not reproduce would change working code on a guess. WHAT WOULD UNBLOCK IT: a screenshot of the wrong counter, plus which step the screen was actually on and how it was reached (clicked through in one session, or landed on after a reload). A reload is the untested path — it re-enters through getInitialStep() in app/(merchant)/products/[id]/page.tsx, which returns 1 only when the merchant has no merchant_products row at all. CARRIED into the W3 packet as an open item, not a defect: the review checklist asks Ivan to screenshot the wrong counter IF he sees it again and to say how he got there, which is the one observation that would make it actionable. APPROVED 2026-08-21 by Ivan: filing this as reported-and-not-reproducible, and blocking it on a second observation rather than inventing a fix, was the right call. CLOSED CANNOT-REPRODUCE 2026-08-21, and the explanation is better than "could not find it": the original sighting was on a page Chrome had auto-translated. Chrome translate REWRITES DOM TEXT in place, so what was on screen was not what the component rendered. That reconciles the two observations that could not both be true: the harness walked 4 -> 5 -> 6 correctly, the code has no literal step number anywhere, and Ivan genuinely saw a wrong number. THE INVESTIGATION HOLDS UP AS A DECISION, not just as luck: blocking on a second observation rather than editing working code on a guess was the right call, and a fabricated "fix" would have changed correct code and left the real cause — a browser extension rewriting the page — undiagnosed and free to do the same thing to any other number on any other screen. ONE, the Redirect URL allowlist (Authentication → URL Configuration) must contain the callback the reset link returns to, `<NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL>/api/auth/callback`. If the project is still on Supabase’s built-in sender it is rate-limited to a handful of messages an hour, which is fine for recovery volume but worth knowing before testing it repeatedly. cards.title: Gate the Supplement Facts panel and its admin editor to the supplements category. Today both are gated on data presence, so a cosmetic with facts filled in renders a supplement label

Also closes the audit finding "Supplement Facts shown on a cosmetic product". WHAT IS WRONG TODAY: components/merchant/product-detail-tabs.tsx renders <SupplementFactsPanel> on `supplement_facts &&` — presence of data, not category — in BOTH the overview and details tabs. components/admin/product-form.tsx and product-edit-form.tsx show the Supplement Facts section unconditionally. Conditional by category, in both the admin editor and the merchant render. RE-DERIVE BEFORE BUILDING: this note names the shape, not the final file list. Confirm both tabs and both admin forms against live code. DATA IS NOT DESTROYED by this card. Facts already stored on a non-supplement product stop RENDERING; nothing is deleted, so a mis-categorised product recovers by having its category corrected rather than by re-typing its facts. It now takes the product category as a prop and derives the facts from it, which gates BOTH tabs that render the panel in one line rather than two conditionals that could disagree. NEGATIVE ARM, which is the whole point of this card: the harness renders the SAME supplement-facts payload under all three categories. supplements shows the panel; cosmeticos and cafe show nothing. Identical data, different category, panel absent — that is the audit finding closed, not merely a conditional added.

cards.title: When a merchant re-adds a product they deleted, offer an explicit choice: reuse the previous label, or start blank
cards.notes: P1 · Created 2026-08-21 from Adam’s ruling via Ivan, following FEAT-merchant-product-delete which shipped on the same review. WHAT HAPPENS TODAY: the soft delete leaves the row in place, and saveMerchantProductAction finds it by the (merchant_id, product_id) pair and clears deleted_at. So a re-add silently REVIVES the old label, mockup and price. That is not a bug — the unique constraint deliberately stays whole because six call sites resolve that pair with .maybeSingle() — but it is a decision made for the merchant without telling them. WHAT THE RULING ADDS: revive stays the behaviour, and the merchant is told and given a choice. "Usar etiqueta anterior" versus start blank. THE CHOICE ONLY EXISTS WHEN THERE IS SOMETHING TO REUSE: a re-add with no stored label has nothing to offer, so the prompt must not appear at all rather than appearing with an empty option. STARTING BLANK IS A CLEAR, NOT A DELETE: it must clear label_url, label_status and mockup_url on the revived row rather than inserting a second row, because the unique constraint forbids the second row and that is exactly why the revive path exists. RE-DERIVE the create-flow entry point before building: app/(merchant)/products/[id]/page.tsx computes initialStep from the merchant_products row, and that row is currently filtered by deleted_at is null, so the deleted row is invisible to the page but visible to the save action. That asymmetry is where the choice has to be surfaced. BUILT 2026-08-21 in PR #40. UI card: in_flight awaiting a final Ivan + Adam pass. WHERE THE CHOICE LIVES, and it is exactly the asymmetry the card predicted: /products/[id] reads the LIVE row (deleted_at is null), so a deleted product is invisible to the page while still being found by saveMerchantProductAction, which would revive it silently. The page now looks for the deleted row too and, when it finds one WITH a stored label, renders the choice instead of the stepper. THE PROMPT DOES NOT APPEAR WHEN THERE IS NOTHING TO REUSE. A deleted row with no label falls straight through to a fresh stepper at step 1, and the existing save path revives the empty row invisibly — which is correct, because there is nothing to tell the merchant about. STARTING BLANK IS A CLEAR, NOT A DELETE, and not an insert either. reviveBlankAction updates the same row: deleted_at null, is_active true, and label_url, label_status, label_rejection_reason and mockup_url reset. Inserting a second row is not available — the unique (merchant_id, product_id) constraint forbids it, which is precisely why the revive path exists — and clearing rather than deleting is what keeps the order history hanging off that row intact. Both actions are scoped .eq(merchant_id) on the lookup AND on the update, so a guessed product id cannot reopen someone else’s row. PDF LABELS get a document chip rather than a broken img, same as the two uploaders and the admin lightbox. VERIFIED in an isolation harness: both states render, the PDF case shows the chip, and the action REFUSES server-side rather than silently succeeding — the harness has no session, so it returns "No autenticado" and the prompt surfaces it. The downstream "Producto no encontrado" guard is unreachable without a session and is stated as unproven rather than claimed. WHAT IS LEFT FOR THE REVIEW PASS: the round trip on a real account. Delete a product, re-add it from the catalog, confirm the prompt appears with the right label, take "usar etiqueta anterior" and confirm the flow resumes at the review step, then delete and re-add again taking "empezar de cero" and confirm the label is gone and the stepper starts at step 3.
